correctness.rationale: At the reflected bond j=-i-1, the complemented particle pair is still (1,0), the gate index evaluates to the original i+delta, and the autonomous obstacle flip at i is mapped to the same kind of flip at 2delta-1-i. These identities hold modulo L, including L=2, and preserve zero rates as well as positive ones. The map squares to the identity and preserves event marks up to the bond permutation; paired event clocks therefore give pathwise equality of all total counts under mapped initial laws. Irreducibility follows by clearing obstacles, moving the particles, and setting the new obstacle pattern. In the all-clear particle graph the in- and outdegrees agree (the numbers of 01 and 10 adjacencies on the ring), and the underlying undirected graph is connected by adjacent swaps. A balanced weakly connected digraph is strongly connected. Empty/full sectors have only obstacle flips. Thus stationary laws correspond. The tilted generators likewise correspond, with bond tilts relabelled; bounded rates give finite finite-time exponential moments, and the finite irreducible tilted generators give the SCGF for real tilts. No equality is asserted for arbitrary unrelated nonstationary initial laws.
residual_risks: The result does not apply to general occupancy-dependent, inhomogeneous or open-boundary obstacle processes; it does not determine the value of the stationary current.

evidence: Ayyer–Misra give equal mapped transition rates for the undeformed K-exclusion dynamics, and distinguish those rates from their stationary symmetry at general deformation.
The indexed reciprocal-deformation extension concerns capacity-constrained occupancies and their hop rates, not an independently evolving gate at every site.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A general marked-generator isomorphism yields path-count equality once its rate conditions are established; it does not identify a field reflection for this model. Increasing capacity does not add the independent obstacle bits and transitions, so the specific earlier K-exclusion results do not give a stronger covering theorem.

exact_database_or_table.reasoning: A tabulated or plotted current (even if exactly symmetric at several sizes) gives only first-moment information and cannot determine a joint multi-time counting law for every ring. The marked-path theorem is not a new numerical table.

originality.rationale: The exact finite-ring marked-process conjugacy, not the already observed mean-current symmetry, is the supported distinction. The two primary defect models are genuinely overlapping, but their inspected passages use or conjecture mean symmetry without the obstacle-index map. The closest indexed structural analogue has different configuration space, rate structure and parameter transformation and does not subsume autonomous obstacles.
residual_risks: Bounded indexed and literature comparisons are not proof of priority; a general model with autonomous reflected bond environments could contain the argument in a different formulation.

value.rationale: Answers a documented unexplained symmetry for a standard interacting-particle model and identifies why the gate placement matters. The exact all-time law yields directly testable complementary-density equalities for current fluctuations, not just another derivation of a numerical curve.
residual_risks: The contribution is the symmetry mechanism and its counting consequences, not a closed current formula or invariant measure.
